title: Space around an office chair

paired_case.title: Space around an office chair
paired_case.question: Does the route from tool storage to the therapist desk pass too close to an occupied chair?
paired_case.grounding: A native Genie office places tool storage and the therapist desk on opposite sides. A BEHAVIOR chair with a visibly seated occupant obstructs the intervening corridor. Direct navigation requests the desk while preserving the source-prescribed 1 m chair clearance. Via-chair navigation must enter the chair-side passing region before continuing to the same desk, using the common physical collision margins. These are explicit action groundings, not learned human avoidance. The v2 planner searches paths and docking poses. Both plans share the complete initial geometry. Clearance is measured from a 0.29 m chassis disc to the measured chair footprint. Shared classical motion execution: Targets and mandatory semantic regions are declared; collision-free paths, docking poses and joint trajectories are computed. Reference labels are never planner inputs. Physical avoidance can prevent a source-plan hazard.
paired_case.limits: The source describes exposure below 0.5 m and recommends at least 1 m clearance. These are different criteria, using an explicit uncalibrated chassis-to-chair distance convention. The seated character and conservative body colliders are static. Human reactions, balance, falls and injury are not simulated. A close pass is exposure evidence, not an injury outcome.
